opts: The commonest cause of hospital AKI
The rarest cause of hospital AKI
items.exp: Pre-renal AKI is marked as the commonest cause of hospital AKI, with the causes grouped from intravascular volume depletion to compartment syndrome. (Book p796)

items.q: Match each pre-renal cause with its category — 1) Hemorrhage/blood loss  2) Cirrhosis  3) Cardiorenal syndrome  4) Sepsis … A) ↓Cardiac output  B) Widespread systemic vasodilation  C) Reduced effective intravascular volume  D) Intravascular volume depletion
items.exp: Pre-renal causes: intravascular volume depletion (haemorrhage, upper GI bleeding, vomiting/diarrhoea, NG loss, diuretic overuse, diabetes insipidus); reduced effective intravascular volume (cirrhosis, cardiac failure, hypoalbuminemia/nephrotic syndrome, third-space sequestration); ↓cardiac output (cardiorenal syndrome); systemic vasodilation (sepsis). (Book p796)

items.q: All but one of the following are causes of intravascular volume depletion in pre-renal AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Cirrhosis acts through reduced effective intravascular volume (splanchnic vasodilation), not true volume depletion, which is caused by haemorrhage, GI losses, diuretics and diabetes insipidus. (Book p796)

items.q: A patient with cirrhosis has a rising creatinine. The proposed mechanism in the list of pre-renal causes is:
opts: Reduced effective intravascular volume due to splanchnic vasodilation
Acute tubular necrosis from bile pigments
True intravascular volume depletion from haemorrhage
items.exp: Pre-renal AKI group 2: reduced effective intravascular volume — cirrhosis (due to splanchnic vasodilation), cardiac failure and hypoalbuminemia/nephrotic syndrome. (Book p796)

items.q: Fill up: In the pre-renal causes list, burns, rhabdomyolysis and acute pancreatitis are grouped under ______ sequestration.
items.exp: Reduced effective intravascular volume from third-space sequestration is bracketed to list burns, rhabdomyolysis and acute pancreatitis. (Book p796)

items.q: A patient with acute pancreatitis develops oliguric AKI. Which group of pre-renal causes covers this?
items.exp: Burns, rhabdomyolysis and acute pancreatitis are grouped under third-space sequestration, a component of reduced effective intravascular volume. (Book p796)

items.q: Match the renal vasoconstriction causes — 1) Hepatorenal syndrome  2) Hypercalcemia  3) Drugs … A) Hepatorenal syndrome  B) NSAIDs, calcineurin inhibitors, ACEi/ARBs  C) Hypercalcemia
items.exp: Renal vasoconstriction (pre-renal cause 5): hepatorenal syndrome, hypercalcemia and drugs — NSAIDs, calcineurin inhibitors and ACE inhibitors/ARBs. (Book p796)

items.q: Fill up: Among the drugs causing pre-renal AKI by renal vasoconstriction, the book lists NSAIDs, calcineurin inhibitors and ______/ARBs.
items.exp: Renal vasoconstriction drugs: NSAIDs, calcineurin inhibitors and ACEi/ARBs — all impair renal autoregulation. (Book p796)

items.q: Sepsis produces pre-renal AKI by widespread systemic vasodilation.
items.exp: Pre-renal cause 4: widespread systemic vasodilation — sepsis. (Book p796)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed pre-renal causes of AKI. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Pre-renal causes listed include diabetes insipidus, cardiorenal syndrome and compartment syndrome (cause 6). Renal lymphoma is a renal (AIN by infiltration) cause. (Book p796)
